metadata.note: The Richmond, Nicholasville, Irvine and Beattyville ("Riney-B") built Versailles - Nicholasville - Richmond - Irvine in 1890 to reach the eastern Kentucky coalfield; bankrupt in 1891, it was sold at foreclosure and conveyed on 19 Aug 1899 to the Louisville and Atlantic, which extended it Irvine - Beattyville in Nov 1902. The L&N bought the L&A's securities 1 Jul 1909 and took the property 1 Nov 1909; from 1 May 1911 its new Millville - Versailles extension joined the Kentucky Highlands distillery line from Frankfort, giving through trains Frankfort - Versailles - Richmond - Irvine - Beattyville. After the 1916 Winchester - Irvine low-grade line the old L&A west of Irvine became a local, and Millville - Irvine was abandoned 30 Sep 1932. Irvine - Beattyville is still CSX's EK Subdivision. Five features: Versailles - Irvine in three eras (RNI&B 1893-1899, L&A 1899-1909, L&N 1909-1931 [OPEN]) sharing identical geometry; L&N Frankfort - Versailles 1911-1931 [OPEN]; L&N Irvine - Beattyville 1911-1951 [OPEN].
metadata.ownership_split: RNI&B -> L&A at the 19 Aug 1899 conveyance (after the 1 May 1899 foreclosure sale); the RNI&B receivership from 2 Dec 1891 is not a split. L&A -> L&N at the 1 Nov 1909 property conveyance; the 1 Jul 1909 stock purchase did not change who ran the trains. The Kentucky Highlands' 31 Jul 1915 conveyance to the L&N is not a split: the L&N ran all passenger trains on it from 1911.
metadata.omitted: Not drawn (drawable NONE or single-year anchors for non-L&A lines): [5] L&A Irvine - Beattyville 1902-1909 (no L&A passenger train confirmed east of Irvine); [7] L&N Winchester - Irvine low-grade line (1951 anchor only; an L&N Eastern Kentucky line, not L&A); [8] L&N Beattyville - Maloney connection (1951 anchor only; L&N-built 1916); [9] Kentucky Highlands Frankfort - Millville 1908-1911 (no passenger evidence before the 1911 through service); [10] Beattyville - Airedale (Beattyville Junction), ex-Winchester & Beattyville / Beattyville & Cumberland Gap (no passenger year); [11] Heidelberg - Ida May (Sturgeon Creek Branch; no passenger year - its 1935 discontinuance is an abandonment date, not a passenger end). RNI&B passenger years 1890-1892 withheld (1893 is the first primary-source year).
metadata.freight_only_check: No freight-only years drawn. Cliffside - Millville was a distillery freight spur after 30 Sep 1932 (to c.1990-95, lifted 1999); Irvine - Beattyville carries CSX coal traffic after the end of passenger service; Heidelberg - Ida May was a coal branch - none of that is drawn.
conflicts: Foreclosure date: Sulzer (via abandonedonline) "sold under foreclosure in 1896"; ICC valuation "Sold at foreclosure, May 1, 1899". Possibly a decree and a later sale; does not affect the drawn years (the RNI&B/receiver ran the trains until the 19 Aug 1899 conveyance).

Kentucky Highlands control: Sulzer says the L&N acquired it in 1909 and built the extension (opened 1 May 1911); KSHS says the L&A acquired it (1909 in one passage, 1911 in another) and built Versailles - Millville "in 1909"; ICC says it was conveyed to the L&N 31 Jul 1915. Immaterial to the draw - no passenger train is confirmed on it until the L&N's 1911 through service.

Mileage: Versailles - Irvine 60.75 mi (Sulzer) vs 62.6 mi (Fowler line 28 mileposts); Irvine - Beattyville 34.75 mi (Sulzer) vs 33.9 mi (Fowler line 4). The traces (see geometry_quality) sit closer to Sulzer for the first and to Fowler for the second.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] ends: L&N Versailles - Irvine and L&N Frankfort - Versailles both end at 1931, the last year a source (Fowler's 1931 public-timetable stops) confirms trains - the line was abandoned 30 Sep 1932 but the last passenger train is not dated by any source checked. L&N Irvine - Beattyville ends at 1951 (Sept 1951 Official Guide Table 27); the 1955-56 end of the Lexington - Hazard trains is not verified. Also unsourced: the RNI&B passenger start (1890 per Sulzer; drawn from 1893, the first primary touch); whether the L&A ran passenger trains Irvine - Beattyville Nov 1902 - 1909 (a c.1910 Courier-Journal timetable on newspapers.com page 118761556 could settle it and the exact date the L&N took over the timetable); how the 1911-1916 through trains reached Jackson/Hazard from Beattyville, if they did; all headways after the RNI&B's "two daily each way" and the 1920 two round trips; all avg_speed_kmh except the 1951 Irvine - Beattyville figure.
metadata.existing_layer_note: Out of scope here, flagged for the owner of lexington_eastern_railway.geojson: its L&N feature "Louisville and Nashville: Lexington – Fleming (Eastern Kentucky Division)" is drawn 1912-1956 on the old Kentucky Union alignment Winchester - Clay City - Beattyville Junction, but the Sept 1951 Guide Table 27 routes Nos. 3/4 Winchester - Irvine - Ravenna - Beattyville - St. Helens, i.e. over the 1916 Winchester - Irvine line and the ex-L&A. So for at least 1951 (very probably from 1916) that feature draws the wrong alignment between Winchester and the Beattyville area. Not changed by this layer.

segments.note: RNI&B ("Riney-B") passenger trains Versailles - Sunol - Keene - Nicholasville - Valley View (Kentucky River high bridge; Marble Creek tunnel) - Million - Richmond - Rice Station - Irvine, connecting with the Louisville Southern at Versailles and crossing the Cincinnati Southern at Nicholasville Junction. START 1893: the first year a primary source touches the line - Fowler marks Garrett, Hispaniola and Rice from the 1893 Official Guide. The line was completed in 1890 and Sulzer says it ran two passenger trains daily each way, but the year passenger service began (possibly piecemeal 1889-90) is not dated by any primary source, so 1890-1892 are withheld, not denied. Receivership from 2 Dec 1891 (same company, receiver operating - not an operator change). Sold at foreclosure 1 May 1899 (ICC; Sulzer says 1896 - conflict recorded in metadata) and conveyed to the Louisville and Atlantic 19 Aug 1899. Headway 720 = Sulzer's "two daily passenger trains in each direction" (secondary source, not a timetable).
sources: Segment-level: Fowler, Kentucky Railroads line 28 (letter z = 1893 Official Guide at Garrett, Hispaniola, Rice) for the 1893 start; Sulzer via abandonedonline for 1890 completion and two trains daily; ICC valuation (via Wikipedia) for the 1 May 1899 foreclosure and 19 Aug 1899 conveyance to the L&A.

segments.note: Louisville and Atlantic operation of the former RNI&B, from the conveyance of 19 Aug 1899 to the conveyance of the property to the Louisville and Nashville on 1 Nov 1909 (ICC). The L&N's purchase of the L&A stocks and bonds on 1 Jul 1909 did not change who ran the trains. Fowler's line-specific letter a (1905 Official Guide) at Versailles, Sunol, Pinckard, Keene, Nicholasville, Valley View, Million, Richmond, Panola, Rice Station and Irvine confirms passenger trains in 1905; 1899-1904 and 1906-1909 rest on continuity with the RNI&B service and with the L&N trains after 1909 - no break in service is reported anywhere. From Nov 1902 the L&A also reached Beattyville, but no source checked confirms L&A passenger trains east of Irvine, so that extension is not drawn for this era. An unverified c.1910 Courier-Journal timetable is said to list the line under the L&A name; if so, the operator change may fall in 1910. Headway 720 is an estimate carried over from the RNI&B's two trains each way; not sourced for this era.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler, Kentucky Railroads line 28 (letter a = 1905 Official Guide) for 1905 service; ICC valuation (via Wikipedia) for the 19 Aug 1899 and 1 Nov 1909 conveyance dates. Frequency not sourced.

segments.note: L&N operation of the ex-Louisville and Atlantic from the property conveyance of 1 Nov 1909. From 1 May 1911 through trains ran Beattyville - Irvine - Richmond - Versailles - Frankfort (Sulzer), and in 1920 the L&N ran two round trips Louisville - Frankfort - (former L&A) - Hazard (Kentucky Streetcar Historical Society). After the L&N's Winchester - Irvine low-grade line opened 14 May 1916 the line was downgraded to local service. Fowler records 1914 working-timetable stops and stops named in a 1931 L&N public timetable (Shanklin, Whitlock, Estrada, Meadow Brook on this stretch). [OPEN] END: passenger service is confirmed to 1931 by that 1931 public timetable. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - the line Millville - Irvine was abandoned 30 Sep 1932, and an unverified summary says the last scheduled train ran that day, but no source checked dates the last passenger train. Do not extend without evidence. Headway 720 is the 1920 figure (two round trips) applied across the era; service after 1916 was a local and may have been thinner - estimate. The Valley View bridge stood unused until scrapped in early 1942; nothing after 1931 is drawn.
sources: Segment-level: ICC valuation (via Wikipedia) for the 1 Nov 1909 conveyance; Sulzer via abandonedonline for 1 May 1911 through trains and the 30 Sep 1932 abandonment; Kentucky Streetcar Historical Society (2010) for the 1920 two round trips; Fowler line 28 (1914 working TT, 1931 public TT stops) for the 1931 [OPEN] end.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced Frankfort - Versailles on OHM/OSM with one short straight leg: 16.2 mi drawn against 16.3 mi documented (Fowler line 28, Frankfort 0.0 - Versailles 16.3) and 16.0 mi by Sulzer (Kentucky Highlands 6.5 + L&N extension 9.5). Routed miles: OHM "Louisville & Nashville R. R." 9.4, OHM "Kentucky Highland Railroad" 4.4, OSM abandoned L&N grade 1.2, live L&N track 0.4, untagged 0.2. STRAIGHT-LINE LEG: the last 0.6 mi at Versailles, from the end of the traced 1911 grade (west side of town, OSM/OHM both stop there) to the start of the Versailles - Irvine feature - the junction itself is not mapped in OSM or OHM. Frankfort end: the line begins on the L&N Louisville - Lexington track near the Frankfort station and runs the 1.0 mi to Cliffside on that main line, which ln_louisville_frankfort_lexington.geojson also draws (shortest overlap that reaches Frankfort). Waypoints: Frankfort and Millville Nominatim (types checked); Cliffside, Glens Creek and Hereford hand-pinned (Nominatim gave Ashland, a Washington Co. cemetery and a Louisville street) - all within 0.5 km of the line except Versailles town centre (0.4-1.2 km). ALIGNMENT ERA: OHM tags this grade from 1907/1911, the era drawn; no relocation is known.

segments.note: Frankfort - Cliffside (on the L&N Louisville - Lexington main line) - Glens Creek - Millville (the Kentucky Highlands Railroad of 1907-08, built for the Old Crow and Old Taylor distilleries) - Labrot - Hereford - Versailles (the L&N's 9.5 mi extension up Glenns Creek, opened 1 May 1911, when "through trains were then scheduled to run from Beattyville west to Frankfort" - Sulzer). In 1920 two Louisville - Hazard round trips ran this way (KSHS). No passenger trains are confirmed on Frankfort - Millville before 1911, so 1908-1910 are not drawn. The Kentucky Highlands was a separate corporation until conveyed to the L&N 31 Jul 1915 (ICC; Sulzer says the L&N acquired it in 1909) - the L&N ran the trains throughout, so that is not an operator split. [OPEN] END: Trumbo, Taylorton and Labrot are named in a 1931 L&N public timetable (Fowler), so passenger service is confirmed to 1931. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - Millville - Versailles was abandoned 30 Sep 1932 and no source checked dates the last passenger train. Do not extend without evidence. After 1932 Cliffside - Millville survived only as a distillery freight spur (CSX abandoned it c.1990-95; track lifted 1999) - not drawn. Headway 720 is the 1920 figure applied across the era; estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Sulzer via abandonedonline for the 1 May 1911 opening, through trains and the 1932 abandonment; Fowler line 28 (1914 working TT at Glens Creek, 1931 public TT at Trumbo, Taylorton, Labrot) for the 1931 [OPEN] end; KSHS (2010) for 1920 service; ICC valuation for the 31 Jul 1915 Kentucky Highlands conveyance.

properties.speed_source: Sept 1951 L&N Table 27 times: Beattyville 10 07 to Ravenna 11 14, about 33 mi in 67 min (~47 km/h) for one train; rounded to 45 and applied across the era - earlier speeds not sourced

properties.geometry_quality: Traced on the surviving track with one short straight leg: 33.8 mi drawn Irvine - Beattyville against 33.9 mi documented (Fowler line 4, Irvine 46.2 - Beattyville 80.1) and 34.75 mi by Sulzer - within 1% of Fowler. Routed miles: OSM rail tagged old_railway_operator=L&N (CSX EK Subdivision) 32.6, untagged rail 1.0. STRAIGHT-LINE LEG: the first 0.3 mi at Irvine, joining the end of the Versailles - Irvine feature to the EK Subdivision so the two lines meet at Irvine; the actual junction/station track there is not traced. The trace follows the Kentucky River line's meanders; opstrace's detour limit was raised to 3x chord for this route only, because it is continuous L&N-tagged track the whole way (every routed mile is L&N or untagged rail). Waypoints Irvine, Ravenna, Evelyn, Heidelberg, Beattyville (Nominatim, types checked) all within 0.4 km. ALIGNMENT ERA: this is the present CSX alignment; any relocation between the 1902 construction and 1951 (e.g. at Ravenna yard, built up as the Eastern Kentucky Division headquarters after 1916) was not researched, so earlier years may be drawn on a later alignment in places.

segments.note: The Louisville and Atlantic's Kentucky River extension Irvine - Ravenna - Old Landing - Evelyn - Heidelberg - Beattyville (completed Nov 1902), under the L&N. START 1911: from 1 May 1911 through trains ran Beattyville - Irvine - Versailles - Frankfort (Sulzer). The L&A years 1902-1909 and the L&N years 1909-1910 are NOT drawn: no source checked names a passenger train east of Irvine before 1911. From 14 May 1916 the L&N's new Winchester - Irvine line made this the main line of the Eastern Kentucky Division (Ravenna its headquarters and shops), carrying the Lexington - Winchester - Irvine - Beattyville - Hazard - Fleming trains; in 1920 two Louisville - Hazard round trips also ran via Frankfort and the old L&A (KSHS). The Sept 1951 Official Guide Table 27 still shows Nos. 3/4 with times at Ravenna 11 14, Evelyn f10 44 (flag), Heidelberg f10 2x (flag) and Beattyville 10 07. [OPEN] END: 1951 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - the Lexington - Hazard trains are said to have ended 1955-56 (last run through Jackson reportedly 14 Jun 1956) but that was not checked. Do not extend without evidence. Headway 720 reflects the 1920 two round trips; by Sept 1951 only one train each way (Nos. 3/4) is shown - estimate across the era. Coal freight continues on the line today under CSX; no passenger claim is implied after 1951.
sources: Segment-level: Sulzer via abandonedonline for the 1 May 1911 through trains; KSHS (2010) for 1920; Official Guide Feb 1952 L&N Table 27 (September 1951) times and index entries for the 1951 [OPEN] end. The 1955-56 end (bookhiker.com) is NOT verified.
